content: RBMS1, also known as RNA-binding motif, single-stranded-interacting protein 1, is a protein encoded by the RBMS1 gene in humans. This protein belongs to a small family of proteins that specifically bind to single-stranded DNA or RNA. These proteins are defined by the presence of two ribonucleoprotein consensus sequence (RNP-CS) motifs, known as RNP1 and RNP2. These motifs are conserved regions originally identified in RNA-binding proteins and are essential for DNA-binding activity. RBMS1 proteins are involved in a variety of critical cellular processes, including DNA replication, gene transcription, cell cycle regulation, and programmed cell death (apoptosis). The gene undergoes alternative splicing, resulting in multiple transcript variants that encode different isoforms of the protein. Several of these isoforms have been identified based on their ability to bind to either strand of an upstream regulatory element of the c-myc gene (referred to as MSSPs), their ability to complement cdc2 and cdc13 yeast mutants (known as scr2), or their potential role as a human repressor of transcription for the HIV-1 and IL-2 receptor alpha (ILR-2α) promoters (referred to as YC1). Additionally, a pseudogene corresponding to RBMS1 is located on chromosome 12. RBMS1 has been demonstrated to interact with DNA polymerase alpha 1, a key enzyme involved in DNA replication.
